correctness.rationale: From P=I-sy^T/(s^Ty)+(tI+nu yy^T)ss^T/(s^Ty) and t+nu||y||^2=1 (0<=t<=1), the symmetric 2D block is [[z(1+tq^2), q(z(1-t)-1)/2],[same,1]], q^2=m^-2-1, z=(s^Ty)/||y||^2. Sylvester's criterion gives iff Delta=z(1+tq^2)-q^2(z(1-t)-1)^2/4>0 for universal strict descent. For fixed noncollinear m any angle-only t<1 violates positivity at large z; t=1 violates it at small z. Recomputed exact SPD quadratic A=[[1,sqrt3],[sqrt3,4]]/80, b=(-5/8,0), first step alpha=64, s=(40,0), y=(1/2,sqrt3/2), m=1/2,z=20: strong Wolfe with c1=0.0001,c2=0.9; both source rho=eta=1 give t=nu=1/2, P=[[50,-sqrt3],[10sqrt3,1]], sym determinant -43/4, g1^T(-Pg1)=5/32>0. Local witness shows ascent for a permitted step, not forced convergence failure.
